headline:
One building.
Two reasons to stay.
story: Ember & Ground opened in 2019 in a converted Victorian grain warehouse in Shoreditch. The building had been empty for eleven years. We liked that it still smelled faintly of old wood.

The steakhouse came first — a twenty-six cover room built around a single wood-fired hearth that burns through half a tonne of seasoned oak every week. We age our own beef on-site, source single-farm cuts from three producers we visit twice a year, and cook everything live over fire.

The café opened the following year in the front of the building, facing the street. Different light, different pace, same philosophy: a short list of things done carefully, nothing on the menu that we can't explain.
philosophy: We don't have a walk-in freezer. Everything we use was alive recently.
The fire is on from open to close. We don't use gas to cook.
If a cut isn't ready, it's not on the menu. We pull dishes mid-service.
